nodes.name: Cardinality estimation of a multiset
nodes.statement: Estimate the number $n$ of distinct elements in a large multiset $M$ in a single pass using minimal auxiliary storage and few operations per scanned record.
nodes.statement_clean: Estimate the number of distinct elements in a large multiset in one pass with little memory.

nodes.name: Hash function
nodes.statement: A function $\mathrm{hash}(x): \text{records} \to [0, 2^L - 1]$ mapping records into integers (or binary strings of length $L$) in a sufficiently uniform manner.

nodes.name: Bit function $\mathrm{bit}(y,k)$
nodes.statement: For non-negative integer $y$, $\mathrm{bit}(y,k)$ is the $k$th bit of the binary representation of $y$, so that $y = \sum_{k \geq 0} \mathrm{bit}(y,k) 2^k$.

nodes.name: Position of least significant 1-bit $\rho(y)$
nodes.statement: $\rho(y) = \min\{ k \geq 0 : \mathrm{bit}(y,k) \neq 0 \}$ if $y > 0$, and $\rho(y) = L$ if $y = 0$.

nodes.name: BITMAP vector
nodes.statement: An $L$-bit vector $\mathrm{BITMAP}[0..L-1]$ in which $\mathrm{BITMAP}[i] = 1$ iff some hashed value of an element of $M$ produced $\rho(\mathrm{hash}(x)) = i$ during the scan.

nodes.name: Observable parameter $R$
nodes.statement: $R$ is the position of the leftmost zero in $\mathrm{BITMAP}$ (ranks start at $0$); used as an indicator of $\log_2 n$.

nodes.name: Probabilistic model on $\mathcal{B}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{B}$ is the set of infinite binary strings whose bits are i.i.d. uniform; equivalently, real numbers uniform on $[0,1]$. The functions $\mathrm{bit}$ and $\rho$ extend trivially.

nodes.name: Random variable $R_n$
nodes.statement: $R_n(x_1,\dots,x_n) = r$ iff for all $0 \leq j < r$ there exists $i$ with $\rho(x_i) = j$, and for all $i$, $\rho(x_i) \neq r$.
nodes.statement_clean: $R_n$ is the analogue of $R$ on $n$ i.i.d. samples from $\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: $\nu(n)$ — number of 1-bits
nodes.statement:
$
u(n)$ is the number of ones in the binary representation of $n$; e.g. $
u(13) = 
u((1101)_2) = 3$.

nodes.name: Stochastic averaging
nodes.statement: Use a single hash $h(x)$ to dispatch each record to one of $m$ buckets via $\alpha = h(x) \bmod m$, updating only $\mathrm{BITMAP}_{\alpha}$ with $\lfloor h(x)/m \rfloor$; emulates $m$ independent hashes at the cost of one.

nodes.name: Standard error and bias
nodes.statement: The standard error of an estimator of $n$ is $\sigma(\hat{n})/n$; the bias is $\lim_{n \to \infty} E[\hat{n}]/n$ (neglecting periodic fluctuations of amplitude $< 10^{-5}$).

nodes.name: Mellin transform
nodes.statement: For $f$ defined on $[0,\infty)$, $f^*(s) = \mathcal{M}[f(x); s] = \int_0^\infty f(x) x^{s-1} dx$, defined in a strip determined by the asymptotics of $f$ at $0$ and $\infty$.
nodes.origin_citation: De Bruijn; see Knuth, AOCP Vol. 3

nodes.name: Auxiliary function $\psi(x)$
nodes.statement: $\psi(x) = \sum_{j \geq 1} (-1)^{\nu(j)+1} e^{-jx}$, used to express the limiting distribution of $R_n$.

nodes.name: Function $F(x)$
nodes.statement: $F(x) = \sum_{k \geq 1} \psi(x/2^k)$; the asymptotic expansion of $F$ governs the mean of $R_n$ via $\bar{R}_n \sim F(n)$.

nodes.name: Entire function $N(s)$
nodes.statement: $N(s) = \sum_{j \geq 1} (-1)^{\nu(j)+1} j^{-s}$, the Dirichlet generating function of the Morse-Thue sequence; analytic continuation gives the Mellin transform of $\psi$.

nodes.name: Magic constant $\varphi$
nodes.statement: $\varphi = 0.77351\ldots$ — the correction factor entering the estimator $\hat{n} = (1/\varphi) \, 2^R$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 — Distribution of $R_n$
nodes.statement: $\Pr[R_n \geq k] = q_{n,k}$ admits the closed-form expansion $q_{n,k} = \sum_{t} (-1)^{t+1} \binom{?}{?}$ derived via inclusion-exclusion on the events $E_j = \{\rho = j\}$ and $K_k = \{\rho \geq k\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Exact closed-form expression for $\Pr[R_n \geq k]$ via inclusion-exclusion.
assumptions: $n$ i.i.d. samples from $\mathcal{B}$ under the uniform model
nodes.notes: PDF math is partially garbled; exact polynomial form is the inclusion-exclusion expansion of $(E_0+\cdots+E_{k-1}+K_k)^n$ over the disjoint pattern events.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Inclusion-exclusion on the disjoint events $E_0,\dots,E_{k-1},K_k$, expanding the non-commutative polynomial $P_k^{(n)} = (E_0+\cdots+E_{k-1}+K_k)^n$ and removing monomials missing some $E_j$.

nodes.name: Set up disjoint events $E_j, K_k$
nodes.statement: Define $E_j = \{\rho = j\}$ for $0 \leq j < k$ and $K_k = \{\rho \geq k\}$; these form a complete disjoint partition of $\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: Expand $P_k^{(n)} = (E_0+\cdots+E_{k-1}+K_k)^n$
nodes.statement: Treat as a non-commutative polynomial; each monomial of degree $n$ corresponds to a disjoint elementary event in $\mathcal{B}^n$.

nodes.name: Apply inclusion-exclusion to remove monomials missing some $E_j$
nodes.statement: $Q_k^{(n)} = P_k^{(n)} - \sum_i P[E_i \to 0] + \sum_{i<j} P[E_i,E_j \to 0] - \cdots$ to count only outcomes with $R_n \geq k$.

nodes.name: Take measure $\mu$ via independence
nodes.statement: Apply $\mu(A \cdot B) = \mu(A)\mu(B)$ on independent trials, change summation indices $\ell_j = k - i_j$, and obtain the announced closed form for $q_{n,k}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 — Asymptotic distribution of $R_n$
nodes.statement: (i) If $k \leq \log_2 n - 2 \log_2 \log n$ then $q_{n,k} = 1 + o(1)$. (ii) If $k \leq \tfrac{5}{4} \log_2 n$ then $q_{n,k} = \psi(n/2^k) + O(\log^6 n / n)$. (iii) For $k \geq \tfrac{5}{4} \log_2 n + \delta$ with $\delta \geq 0$, $q_{n,k} = O(2^{-\delta}/\sqrt{n})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Three-regime asymptotics for $\Pr[R_n \geq k]$ giving the limiting profile $\psi(n/2^k)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Use the exponential approximation $(1 - 1/2^k)^n \approx e^{-n/2^k}$ termwise, truncate the inclusion-exclusion sum at $j \leq \varepsilon(n) 2^k$, control the tail bound, then complete the sum to the entire $\psi$.

nodes.name: Three regimes by size of $k$ vs $\log_2 n$
nodes.statement: Split into (i) small $k$ where $q_{n,k} \to 1$, (ii) moderate $k$ where the limiting profile $\psi$ governs, (iii) large $k$ where binomial tail is exponentially small.

nodes.name: Exponential approximation of terms $t(j,n,k)$
nodes.statement: Set $t(j,n,k) = (1 - j/2^k)^n$ and replace by $e^{-nj/2^k}$ with error $O(nj^2/2^{2k})$; valid uniformly for $j < \varepsilon(n) 2^k$.

nodes.name: Complete the sum to $\psi$
nodes.statement: Add back the negligible tail of $\sum_{j \geq 0}(-1)^{\nu(j)} e^{-nj/2^k}$ and simplify using the product identity $\sum_{j\geq 0}(-1)^{\nu(j)} q^j = \prod_{m \geq 0}(1 - q^{2^m})$.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 — $\bar{R}_n \sim F(n)$
nodes.statement: The expectation $\bar{R}_n = E[R_n]$ satisfies $\bar{R}_n = F(n) + o(1)$ where $F(x) = \sum_{k \geq 1} \psi(x/2^k)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2 — Mellin transform of $F$
nodes.statement: For $-1 < \mathrm{Re}(s) < 0$, $F^*(s) = \Gamma(s) N(s) / (1 - 2^s)$, where $N(s)$ is the Dirichlet generating function (entire continuation) of the Morse-Thue signs.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Compute $\psi^*$ using the functional property $\mathcal{M}[f(ax);s] = a^{-s} f^*(s)$ and the fact that $\mathcal{M}[e^{-x};s] = \Gamma(s)$, then sum the geometric series in $k$ to obtain $F^*(s)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3 — Properties of $N(s)$
nodes.statement: $N(0) = -1$ and for $s = \sigma + it$ with $\sigma > -0.99$, $N(s) = O(1 + |s|^3)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Group terms of $N(s)$ in blocks of four using $\nu(4j+r)$ identities, split the sum at $j = |s|^2$, and bound each piece; substitute $s=0$ for $N(0) = -1$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.A — Mean of $R_n$
nodes.statement: $\bar{R}_n = \log_2(\varphi n) + P(\log_2 n) + o(1)$, where $\varphi = 0.77351\ldots$ is given via $N$ and $P(u)$ is a continuous periodic function with period $1$ and amplitude $< 10^{-5}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.A
nodes.statement: Apply Mellin inversion of $F^*$ on a rectangular contour; the double pole at $s=0$ contributes the dominant $\log_2 \varphi n$ term, simple poles at $\chi_k = 2ik\pi/\log 2$ give the periodic Fourier series $P(u)$.

nodes.name: Mellin inversion contour $\Gamma_k$
nodes.statement: Define rectangle with vertical sides at $\mathrm{Re}(s) = -1/2$ and $\mathrm{Re}(s) = 1$, horizontal sides at heights $\pm (2k+1)\pi/\log 2$.

nodes.name: Vanishing of horizontal segments
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 3 plus exponential decrease of $\Gamma(s)$ towards $\pm i\infty$ to show horizontal contour pieces contribute $\to 0$ as $k \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Sum residues at $s=0$ and at $\chi_k = 2ik\pi/\log 2$
nodes.statement: Double pole at $s=0$ gives $\log_2 \varphi n$ via $\gamma/\log 2 + N'(0)/\log 2 - 1/2$; simple poles at $\chi_k$ give Fourier coefficients $P_k$.

nodes.name: Assemble Fourier series $P(u) = \sum P_k e^{-2ik\pi u}$
nodes.statement: Sum residues over $\mathrm{Re}(s) = 0$ to assemble the periodic continuous function $P(u)$ of amplitude $< 10^{-5}$ (Appendix gives the bound).

nodes.name: Theorem 3.B — Standard deviation of $R_n$
nodes.statement: $\sigma_n^2 = \sigma_\infty^2 + Q(\log_2 n) + o(1)$ with $\sigma_\infty = 1.12127\ldots$ and $Q(u)$ a periodic mean-zero function of period $1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.B
nodes.statement: Let $G(n) = \sum_{k \geq 1} k^2 \psi(n/2^k) - F(n)^2$ approximate $S_n - \bar{R}_n^2$; compute $G^*(s)$ which has a triple pole at $s=0$, and apply residue calculus.

nodes.name: COUNT — Basic probabilistic counting procedure
nodes.statement: Maintain $\mathrm{BITMAP}[0..L-1]$; for each $x$ in $M$ set $\mathrm{BITMAP}[\rho(\mathrm{hash}(x))] := 1$; output $R$ = position of leftmost $0$.
output: Integer $R$, position of leftmost $0$ in $\mathrm{BITMAP}$, used as estimator of $\log_2 \varphi n$
nodes.pseudocode: for i := 0 to L-1 do BITMAP[i] := 0; for all x in M do begin index := rho(hash(x)); if BITMAP[index] = 0 then BITMAP[index] := 1; end; R := position of leftmost 0 in BITMAP

nodes.name: Zero $\mathrm{BITMAP}$
nodes.statement: for $i := 0$ to $L-1$ do $\mathrm{BITMAP}[i] := 0$.

nodes.name: Scan $M$ and set bit at $\rho(\mathrm{hash}(x))$
nodes.statement: for all $x \in M$: $\mathrm{index} := \rho(\mathrm{hash}(x))$; if $\mathrm{BITMAP}[\mathrm{index}] = 0$ then $\mathrm{BITMAP}[\mathrm{index}] := 1$.

nodes.name: Return position of leftmost zero $R$
nodes.statement: Output $R := \min\{ k : \mathrm{BITMAP}[k] = 0 \}$, used to estimate $\log_2 (\varphi n)$.

nodes.name: Estimator $\hat{n} = (1/\varphi) 2^R$
nodes.statement: $A(n) = (1/\varphi) 2^{\bar{R}_n}$; e.g. $A(10) = 10.502$, $A(100) = 100.4997$, $A(1000) = 1000.502$, motivating $\hat{n} = (1/\varphi) 2^R$ as a near-unbiased estimator (modulo binary-order dispersion).

nodes.name: Direct averaging — $m$ independent hash functions
nodes.statement: Run COUNT with $m$ independent hash functions to get $R^{(1)},\dots,R^{(m)}$; average $A = (1/m) \sum R^{(i)}$ and output $2^A$. Standard error $\approx \sigma_\infty/\sqrt{m}$.
nodes.notes: Provably good but multiplies CPU per element by $m$.

nodes.name: PCSA — Probabilistic Counting with Stochastic Averaging
nodes.statement: Single hash $h$ dispatches each record to bucket $\alpha = h(x) \bmod m$, updating $\mathrm{BITMAP}[\alpha,\cdot]$ at index $\rho(\lfloor h(x)/m \rfloor)$. Final estimate $E := \mathrm{trunc}(m/\varphi \cdot 2^{S/m})$ where $S = \sum_i R^{(i)}$.
output: Estimate $E$ of cardinality $n = |\{x \in M\}|$ with bias $1 + 0.31/m$ and standard error $\approx 0.78/\sqrt{m}$
nodes.pseudocode: while not eof(M) do begin x := getelement; hashedx := hash(x); a := hashedx mod nmap; index := rho(hashedx div nmap); if BITMAP[a,index] = 0 then BITMAP[a,index] := 1; end; S := 0; for i := 0 to nmap-1 do begin R := 0; while BITMAP[i,R] = 1 and R < maxlength do R := R+1; S := S+R; end; Z := trunc(nmap/varphi * 2**(S/nmap)).

nodes.name: Zero BITMAP matrix and counters
nodes.statement: Allocate $\mathrm{BITMAP}[0..\mathrm{nmap}-1, 0..\mathrm{maxlength}-1]$ initialized to 0, $S := 0$.

nodes.name: Scan: dispatch by $h(x) \bmod m$ and set bit
nodes.statement: For each $x \in M$: $\alpha := h(x) \bmod \mathrm{nmap}$; $\mathrm{index} := \rho(\lfloor h(x)/\mathrm{nmap} \rfloor)$; if $\mathrm{BITMAP}[\alpha, \mathrm{index}] = 0$ then set to $1$.

nodes.name: Aggregate: compute $R^{(i)}$ and sum $S$
nodes.statement: For $i := 0$ to $\mathrm{nmap}-1$ scan $\mathrm{BITMAP}[i,\cdot]$ for the leftmost zero $R$ and accumulate $S := S + R$.

nodes.name: Output $Z := \mathrm{trunc}(\mathrm{nmap}/\varphi \cdot 2^{S/\mathrm{nmap}})$
nodes.statement: Compute final estimate $Z$; for small $\mathrm{nmap}$ apply bias correction $\varphi(1 + 0.31/\mathrm{nmap})$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4 — Asymptotics of $E[\beta^{R_n}]$
nodes.statement: For $\beta = 2^{1/q}$ with $q \geq 1$ fixed, $E[\beta^{R_n}] = n^{1/q}(d_q + P_q(\log_2 n)) + O(n^{0.76/q})$, with $d_q$ the residue of an explicit Mellin transform at $s = -1/q$ and $P_q$ a small periodic fluctuation.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Strengthen tail bounds on $\Pr[R_n > k]$, replace $p_{n,k}$ by their asymptotic equivalents, complete the sum to define $H(n)$ and apply the Mellin transform with poles at $s = -1/q + 2ik\pi/\log 2$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5 — Concentration of bucket loads
nodes.statement: If $n$ elements are distributed into $m$ cells (each cell with probability $1/m$), the probability that some cell has $|N - n/m| > \sqrt{n} \log n$ is $O(e^{-h \log^2 n})$ for some $h > 0$.
assumptions: $n$ elements i.i.d. uniform over $m$ cells, $m$ fixed
conclusions: $\Pr[\exists\text{ cell with } |N - n/m| > \sqrt{n}\log n] = O(e^{-h \log^2 n})$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Use binomial probability $\Pr[N_1 = pn + \delta]$, take logarithms, observe $\delta = \sqrt{n}\log n$ makes the probability exponentially small, and use unimodality plus a union bound over cells.

nodes.name: Theorem 4 — Mean and second moment of PCSA estimator $E_n$
nodes.statement: $E[E_n]$ and $E[E_n^2]$ admit closed-form asymptotic expansions involving $\Gamma$-evaluations $\Gamma(-1/m)$, $N(-1/m)$, $N(-2/m)$, and small periodic functions $P_*, Q_*$ of period $1$ and amplitude $< 10^{-5}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma 4 and Lemma 5: Lemma 5 lets one approximate PCSA as if buckets received exactly $n/m$ elements; Lemma 4 gives the moment $E[2^{R_{n/m}/m}]$ per bucket; multiply over independent buckets via the multinomial expansion of $E[2^{S/m}]$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5 — Bias and standard error of PCSA
nodes.statement: PCSA's bias $\sim 1 + \varepsilon(m)$ and standard error $\sim \eta(m)$ satisfy as $m \to \infty$: bias $\approx 1 + 0.31/m$, standard error $\approx 0.78/\sqrt{m}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5
nodes.statement: Asymptotically expand $\Gamma(-1/m)$, $N(-1/m)$, $N(-2/m)$ for large $m$ (via MACSYMA), neglect the $< 10^{-5}$ periodic fluctuations, and read off the bias and variance constants.

nodes.name: Standard error scaling $\sigma_\infty/\sqrt{m}$
nodes.statement: Direct averaging over $m$ hashes gives $E[A] = \log_2(\varphi n)$ and $\sigma(A) = \sigma_\infty/\sqrt{m}$, so the relative error of $2^A$ is $\approx \sigma_\infty/\sqrt{m}$ (i.e. $\approx 0.78/\sqrt{m}$ for PCSA).

nodes.name: Length of BITMAP rule $L > \log_2(n/m) + 4$
nodes.statement: Because the $R$-distribution is steep, choosing $L > \log_2(n/\mathrm{nmap}) + 4$ keeps truncation error below $5 \times 10^{-5}$; e.g. $\mathrm{nmap}=64, L=16$ supports $n$ up to $10^5$, $L=24$ covers $n \gg 10^7$.

nodes.name: Bias correction for small $m$
nodes.statement: Replace the final instruction by $E := \mathrm{trunc}(\mathrm{nmap}/(\varphi(1 + 0.31/\mathrm{nmap})) \cdot 2^{S/\mathrm{nmap}})$ to obtain an asymptotically unbiased estimator (apart from periodic fluctuations $< 10^{-5}$).

nodes.name: Distributed counting via OR of BITMAPs
nodes.statement: If $F = \bigcup_i F_i$ is partitioned, run PCSA per $F_i$ and OR the BITMAPs at a central processor; accuracy is unaffected by the partition, communication is $O(s)$ messages.

nodes.name: Scrolling encoding
nodes.statement: BITMAP rows have a fringe structure; encode only the boundary plus a window of size $\approx 8$ to reduce storage to $\tfrac{1}{2}\log_2 n + \mathrm{nmap}$ bytes.

nodes.name: Deletions via per-pattern counters
nodes.statement: Replacing bits by counts of pattern occurrences yields an algorithm supporting arbitrary insertion/deletion sequences at the cost of additional storage.

nodes.name: Unix manual BITMAP example ($n = 16405$)
nodes.statement: Volume 1 of the Unix manual: $|M| = 26692$ lines, $16405$ distinct. With $L = 24$ multiplicative hashing, the BITMAP is $111111111111001100000000$, leftmost zero at position $12$, while $2^{14} = 16384$.

nodes.name: PCSA simulations on man$_1,\dots$,man$_8$.w files
nodes.statement: PCSA applied to 16 textual files (chapters of online documentation, with line- and 5-character-block records) under standard multiplicative hashing yields estimates within typical relative error $\approx 0.78/\sqrt{m}$ of the true cardinalities (Tables III, IV).

nodes.name: Morris's approximate counting (cited)
nodes.statement: Morris's algorithm maintains an approximate counter for events with expected constant relative accuracy using only $\log_2 \log_2 n + O(1)$ bits.

nodes.name: Proof of Appendix lemma
nodes.statement: Use $|e^{-iu} - 1 + iu| \leq u^2/2$ on each $\log(1 + jx)$, expand $f$ in exponential form, and estimate the remainder by $14 t^2 x^2$, then add the leading $2 t x^2$ term.

nodes.name: Appendix corollary — bound on $|N(it)|$
nodes.statement: For all $t \geq 1$, $|N(it)| \leq t^2 + 7t + 7$.

nodes.name: Proof of Appendix corollary
nodes.statement: Express $N(it)$ via $f(1/4j, t)$, split the sum at $j_0(t) = \max(\lfloor t/6 \rfloor, 1)$, apply the trivial bound $|f| \leq 4$ on the small-$j$ part and the Lemma's bound $|f| \leq 16 x^2 t^2$ on the large-$j$ part.

nodes.name: Optimal storage/accuracy tradeoff
nodes.statement: Determine whether appreciably better storage/accuracy tradeoffs than $O(m \log_2 n)$ storage with relative error $\sim c/\sqrt{m}$ can be achieved (or prove that no such tradeoff is possible from an information-theoretic standpoint).
